title: What Is Vedanta? The Self and Ultimate Reality
h1: What Is Vedanta? The Self and Ultimate Reality
excerpt: Vedanta is a tradition of interpreting the Upanishads. Advaita, its famous non-dual school, is one reading among others.

quick_answer.question: What is Vedanta?
quick_answer.answer: Vedanta is an Indian philosophical tradition that interprets the Upanishads, the Brahma Sutras, and the Bhagavad Gita. Advaita Vedanta teaches that the self and ultimate reality are not two.

intro: Vedanta names schools that take a small canon seriously and then argue. The argument is the tradition. A sentence on a mug is not.

sections.heading: What texts define Vedanta?
sections.content:
The canon is commonly the Upanishads, the Brahma Sutras, and the Bhagavad Gita. Advaita, associated with Shankara, says the deepest teaching identifies atman and brahman. Ignorance, on this view, makes a separate self seem obvious. Knowledge is said to remove that error. The Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy outlines the school without recruiting you.

The neighboring page is [the Vedanta topic](/topics/vedanta/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: What does Advaita claim?
sections.content:
Other Vedantas deny that the self and the ultimate are simply the same. Qualified non-dual and dual readings are part of the history. If a teacher says Vedanta as if only Advaita existed, you are hearing a party.

A wider map lives at the [ancient wisdom topic](/topics/ancient-wisdom/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: What do other readings refuse?
sections.content:
Study, reflection, and meditation appear in Advaita-influenced teaching, often after ethical preparation that popular extracts skip. You can read a public Upanishad translation without adopting the doctrine. Non-duality is not a reason to neglect people.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [Atman and Brahman](/articles/atman-vs-brahman/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not confuse the doctrine with every app that says you are awareness. An attention skill is not a theory of reality. This page will not call the doctrine a scientific result.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Vedanta is commentary on a canon.
Atman and brahman are technical terms.
The teaching is not a productivity method.
